title: The Reckoning

segments.text: Then, suddenly, the music stopped. In the first week of February 1637, buyers stopped showing up, and prices collapsed.
But here is the real twist: the ruin Mackay described may never have happened.
Historian Anne Goldgar read the archived contracts: the traders were mostly wealthy merchants and craftsmen.
She argues that most accounts rest on a little propaganda and a prodigious amount of plagiarism.
The bubble was real for a few. The legend was written for everyone else.

summary_for_next: Prices collapse in the first week of February 1637; the guild turns contracts into options; Goldgar's archives contest Mackay's ruin.
